worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot {4}^{x} & >7 \\ {4}^{x} & >14.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the logarithm to base $4$ of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{4}⁡({4}^{x}) & >{log}_{4}⁡(14) \\ x & >{log}_{4}⁡(14).\end{aligned}
$$
